extracted.intended_audience: advanced undergraduates and graduate students studying algebraic geometry
extracted.subtask_description: Working through a graduate-level textbook chapter covering regular schemes (regular local rings and their properties), the Artin–Rees lemma and filtered modules, and the definition/characterization and basic properties of quasicoherent and locally free sheaves. The material mixes definitions, theorems, proofs, and exercises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regularity in dimension 1 (Exercise 12.8.A)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppose X is a Noetherian dimension 1 scheme that is regular at its closed points. Show that X is reduced. Hence show (without invoking Fact 12.8.2) that X is regular.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is presented as an exercise the reader can do immediately; it emphasizes proving reducedness first and then deducing regularity in the 1-dimensional Noetherian case where regularity holds at closed points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regularity for finite type schemes over perfect fields (Theorem 12.8.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is a finite type scheme over a perfect field k that is regular at its closed points, then X is regular.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statement of the theorem; the text points to a later proof (21.3.12). Also notes a more general version (Exercise 21.3.G) for localizations of finite type algebras over perfect fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regular local rings are unique factorization domains (Auslander–Buchsbaum Theorem, Fact 12.8.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Regular local rings are unique factorization domains (i.e., regular implies factorial).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marked as a hard theorem; references are given for proofs. Consequence: regular schemes are factorial and hence normal (via Exercise 5.4.F). The author notes they will not use this fact further in the book.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regular local rings are integrally closed (12.8.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Regular local rings are integrally closed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This can be deduced from the Auslander–Buchsbaum theorem (Fact 12.8.5) or proved directly in important geometric cases later (26.3.5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Regular local rings are Cohen–Macaulay (12.8.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Regular local rings are Cohen–Macaulay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This will be shown in the book later (26.2.5); the remark signals this structural property of regular local rings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: I-filtration and I-stable filtration (12.9.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: A descending filtration M = M0 ⊃ M1 ⊃ M2 ⊃ ··· of an A-module M is called an I-filtration if I·Mn ⊂ Mn+1. It is I-stable if for some s and all n,d ≥ 0, Id Ms = Mn+s.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: the I-adic filtration Mk = I^k M is I-stable. The Rees algebra/module construction (A•(I) = ⊕_{n≥0} I^n, M• = ⊕_{n≥0} M_n) is introduced to translate stability into finite generation over graded rings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rees algebra / finite generation criterion (Proposition 12.9.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a filtration (12.9.1.1), the filtration is I-stable iff the associated graded/rees module M• is a finitely generated module over the Rees algebra A•(I).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof outline: if M• is finitely generated over the Noetherian A•(I) then Noetherianness yields stabilization of the filtration; conversely, I-stability gives finite generation of M• by finitely many Mj.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artin–Rees Lemma (12.9.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppose A is a Noetherian ring, M is a finitely generated A-module with an I-stable filtration M = M0 ⊃ M1 ⊃ ···, and L ⊂ M is a submodule. Let Ln := L ∩ Mn. Then the filtration L = L0 ⊃ L1 ⊃ L2 ⊃ ··· is an I-stable filtration of L.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This generalizes the intuition that functions analytically zero at a point vanish in a neighborhood; used later (e.g., Cohomology and Base Change Theorem 28.1.6). Proof uses the Rees-module finite generation criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artin–Rees corollary for powers of ideals (12.9.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: If I is an ideal in a Noetherian ring A, M a finitely generated A-module, and L ⊂ M a submodule, then there exists an integer s such that for all d≥0 one has a stable relation between I^d L and L ∩ I^{d+s} M (i.e., the filtration on L induced from the I-adic filtration of M stabilizes after a shift).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is obtained by applying the Artin–Rees Lemma to the I-adic filtration Mn = I^n M. Warning in text: it need not be true that I^d L = L ∩ I^d M for all d (counterexamples exist).

rubrics_metrics.name: Krull intersection type consequences (12.9.A exercise)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exercises deduce vanishing of intersections like ⋂_{j=1}^∞ I^j M = 0 under Noetherian hypotheses (and for Noetherian integral domains or Noetherian local rings with I proper, ⋂ I^j = 0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hints: apply Artin–Rees with L = ⋂_{j=1}^∞ I^j M and use Nakayama's lemma (first version, Lemma 7.2.8). This yields Proposition 12.5.2 (for Noetherian local rings, ⋂ m^i = 0).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: vector bundle and locally free sheaf (13.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: A rank n vector bundle on a manifold M is a map π: V → M such that π^{-1}(x) is an n-dimensional vector space for each x and locally V|_U ≅ U × R^n via a trivialization. A locally free sheaf of rank n on a ringed space X is an O_X-module locally isomorphic to O_X^n (i.e., corresponds to a vector bundle).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections over a trivializing open are identified with n-tuples of functions. Rank 1 locally free sheaves are invertible sheaves (line bundles). The book emphasizes the equivalence of perspectives (vector bundles ↔ locally free sheaves).

rubrics_metrics.name: Transition functions and cocycle condition (13.1.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given trivializations over an open cover {U_i}, the transition functions T_{ij} ∈ GL_n(O(U_i ∩ U_j)) must satisfy the cocycle condition T_{ij} T_{jk} = T_{ik} on triple overlaps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The data (cover, transition functions satisfying the cocycle condition) is equivalent to specifying the vector bundle / locally free sheaf up to unique isomorphism; gluing is done using these transition matrices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sheaf of sections identification (13.1.2–13.1.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a trivialization over U, sections of the vector bundle over U correspond to n-tuples of functions on U; the sheaf of sections is an O_X-module and is locally free.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 13.1.A asks to check compatibility of local representations: on overlaps the n-tuples are related by the same transition functions Tij.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invertible sheaves and the Picard group (13.1.4, 13.1.G)
rubrics_metrics.description: A rank 1 locally free sheaf is an invertible sheaf (line bundle). Invertible sheaves up to isomorphism form an abelian group under tensor product, called Pic X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercises ask to show duals of invertible sheaves invert the transition functions and to establish functoriality of Pic under pullback (13.1.H).

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic locally free sheaf constructions and exactness (13.1.B–13.1.F)
rubrics_metrics.description: If F and G are locally free sheaves of ranks m and n then Hom_OX(F,G) is locally free of rank mn; the dual E^∨ := Hom(E,O_X) is locally free of same rank; tensoring by a locally free sheaf is exact; for finite-rank locally free E, Hom(F ⊗ E, G) ≅ Hom(F, E^∨ ⊗ G), etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hints: many properties are checked stalkwise. Tensoring by locally free is exact because tensoring by free modules is exact on stalks; exercises guide verifying these canonical isomorphisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subscheme cut out by a section V(s) (Exercise 13.1.I)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a section s of a locally free sheaf F on a scheme X, define the closed subscheme V(s) cut out by s = 0 as the largest closed subscheme on which s restricts to zero; check independence of trivialization choices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hints: locally in a trivialization s corresponds to functions f1,...,fr and one can take the closed subscheme cut out by these functions; alternative coordinate-free largest-closed-subscheme description is suggested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hartogs extension for locally free sheaves (13.1.J)
rubrics_metrics.description: On a locally Noetherian normal scheme, sections of a locally free sheaf defined away from a closed set of codimension at least 2 extend over that set (algebraic Hartogs phenomenon).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise refers to Theorem 11.3.11 for the algebraic Hartogs lemma; this is an extension property for sections of locally free sheaves on normal Noetherian schemes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of quasicoherent sheaf (13.2.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: An O_X-module F on a scheme X is quasicoherent if for every affine open Spec A ⊂ X, F|_{Spec A} ≅ ~M for some A-module M.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theorem 13.2.1 shows it suffices to check this on an affine cover; examples: all locally free sheaves are quasicoherent. Exercises warn that not every O_X-module is quasicoherent (e.g., certain skyscraper sheaves).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quasicoherent sheaf characterized by distinguished affine base (13.3.3 & 13.3.D)
rubrics_metrics.description: An O_X-module F is quasicoherent iff for every distinguished inclusion Spec A_f ⊂ Spec A the natural map Γ(Spec A,F) ⊗_A A_f → Γ(Spec A_f,F) (equivalently Γ(Spec A,F)_f → Γ(Spec A_f,F)) is an isomorphism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This means the module on a distinguished open is obtained by localizing the module on the larger affine open. Exercise 13.3.D asks to show this equivalence and it provides a practical criterion to check quasicoherence using restriction/localization behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguished affine base suffices to recover sheaves (Theorem 13.3.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: A sheaf on the distinguished affine base (affine opens and distinguished inclusions) determines a unique sheaf on X whose restriction to the distinguished base is the given one; morphisms likewise correspond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The theorem says all information of a sheaf is contained in its data on affine opens and distinguished inclusions; proof uses stalks as colimits and the sheaf of compatible germs construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: QCQS lemma for sections and localization (13.3.E)
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is quasicompact and quasiseparated and F is quasicoherent, then for any function f on X the restriction map Γ(X,F) → Γ(X_f,F) is precisely localization at f (i.e., Γ(X,F)_f ≅ Γ(X_f,F)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise suggests using a finite affine cover and exactness (localization is exact) to prove the isomorphism; this is a useful computational property of global sections of QC sheaves on qcqs schemes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples and non-examples of quasicoherent sheaves (13.2.A & 13.2.B)
rubrics_metrics.description: Not every O_X-module is quasicoherent: e.g., on X = Spec k[t], the skyscraper sheaf at the origin with group k(t) is not quasicoherent; but the skyscraper at the generic point with group k(t) (the function field) can be given the structure of a quasicoherent sheaf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercises guide constructing these examples and using them to show not every QC sheaf is locally free. These examples illustrate the distinction between general O_X-modules and quasicoherent ones.
